hook: FastAPI: the framework that made Python APIs feel modern. Type hints become validation, validation becomes docs — **Swagger UI for free**.

scenes.title: Routes: the controllers you already know
scenes.sub: Decorators, path/query params — ASP.NET energy, Python syntax
scenes.narration: If you've written controllers in dot-NET, FastAPI's mental model is instantly familiar. An app object; routes as decorated functions; get, post, put, delete — HTTP verbs mapped to Python functions. Path parameters live in the URL — slash users slash user-id — and double as types: declare user-id as int and FastAPI rejects 'abc' with a clean 422 before your code runs. Query parameters are plain function arguments with defaults — limit equals twenty becomes optional and validated. The philosophy: function SIGNATURES are the contract — types in, types out — and everything else is generated from them.

scenes.title: Routes + Pydantic: the contract IS the code
annot: Pydantic models as request/response: validation, serialization AND docs from one definition
Field(ge=1, le=50): range checks declarative — the 422 responses come free
async def routes: FastAPI runs them on the event loop — await your LLM calls directly
scenes.narration: One file, the whole idea. The request model carries its own constraints — min-length, max-length, range — so malformed input dies at the door with a precise error, not deep in your logic. response-model shapes the OUTGOING contract too: extra fields stripped, types enforced, the API surface stays clean as internals evolve. And note async def: FastAPI endpoints run as coroutines, so awaiting your vector search and LLM calls inside a route is natural — no executor bridging, PY-10 concurrency straight in your controllers. This is why FastAPI became the default for LLM backends: the I/O-heavy shape of GenAI apps fits it perfectly.

scenes.title: Depends(): **DI like .NET**, without the ceremony

lines: with Session() as db: yield db

steps.at: A function declares what it needs

scenes.narration: Dependency injection in FastAPI is a parameter with Depends. A function declares what it needs — a database session, the current user, a rate limiter — as a typed parameter, and FastAPI calls the provider, caches it per-request, and injects the result. The dot-NET comparison is apt: constructor injection becomes function parameters, scopes become the request lifecycle, and everything stays explicit in the signature. Why it matters in practice: cross-cutting needs — auth, sessions, common query building — stop being copy-pasted boilerplate and become named, testable units. And because dependencies are functions, you can OVERRIDE them in tests — swap the real database for a fake without touching route code.

scenes.title: Depends() chains: db session + current user + services
scenes.body:
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from typing import Annotated

async def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db                 # per-request session, auto-closed
    finally:
        db.close()

async def get_current_user(
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
    token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)],
) -> User:
    user = verify_token(token, db)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)
    return user

@app.get("/me/usage")
def my_usage(
    user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],  # full chain
    db:   Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
):
    return db.query(Usage).filter_by(user_id=user.id).all()

# Test override:
# app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: fake_user
# — no auth mocking gymnastics, just replace the provider
annot: Depends chains compose: get_current_user itself Depends on db — FastAPI resolves the whole graph per request
yield dependencies get teardown (finally) — sessions and connections close even on exceptions
dependency_overrides in tests is the payoff: swap providers at the seam, not with monkey-patching
scenes.narration: The dependency graph resolves itself: my-usage needs a user; the user needs a database and a token; FastAPI builds the chain, caches each per request, and tears down yield-dependencies in reverse. Three wins. Testability: dependency-overrides swaps any provider — test routes with a fake user, no token forging. Explicitness: the signature IS the route's requirements — read it and you know exactly what the endpoint needs, unlike middleware where behavior hides. Shared logic without globals: the db session is created once per request and shared everywhere it's injected — no thread-local session hacks. For GenAI apps, inject your vector store client and LLM client the same way — one provider, mocked in tests.

scenes.title: Cross-cutting concerns, background work, live streams

do: words appear as the model writes

scenes.narration: Middleware wraps every request — logging, timing, request-ids — a decorator around the whole app rather than per route. CORS middleware is the one every frontend developer meets: browsers block cross-origin API calls by default, and the middleware whitelists which origins may call you — for a public API, configure origins deliberately, not wildcard-plus-credentials. BackgroundTasks: work that must happen but shouldn't delay the response — audit logging, notifications, cache warming; the response returns, the task completes after. StreamingResponse with server-sent events is the headline act for GenAI: PY-12 taught you to consume LLM token streams; here you RE-EMIT them — the browser shows words appearing as the model generates them.

scenes.title: Middleware + CORS + BackgroundTasks + SSE
scenes.body:
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from sse_starlette.sse import EventSourceResponse
import time, uuid

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["https://myapp.com"],  # NOT "*" with credentials
    allow_methods=["*"],
)

@app.middleware("http")
async def add_request_id(request, call_next):
    request.state.request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = request.state.request_id
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = f"{time.perf_counter()-start:.3f}s"
    return response

async def audit_log(question: str, user_id: str):
    await db.insert("query_log", {"q": question, "user": user_id})

@app.post("/ask")
async def ask(req: AskRequest, background: BackgroundTasks):
    background.add_task(audit_log, req.question, current_user_id())
    return EventSourceResponse(stream_answer(req.question))  # SSE!
annot: Middleware order matters: CORS added last wraps everything — it's applied in REVERSE add order
BackgroundTasks run AFTER the response is sent — perfect for fire-and-forget, NOT for work the response needs
EventSourceResponse is the full loop: LLM streams to you (httpx), you stream to the browser (SSE)
scenes.narration: Four mechanisms, one snippet. Middleware runs around everything — request-id and timing headers become observability you got for free. CORS is deliberate: exact origins, because allow-origins star plus credentials is a security hole browsers warn you about for a reason. BackgroundTasks for genuinely deferrable work — if the response NEEDS the result, it's not a background task, it's just the handler. And EventSourceResponse completes the streaming story: httpx streams tokens from the LLM — PY-12 — your generator yields them, and the browser's EventSource reads them as server-sent events. Time from model token to user screen: milliseconds. That loop — LLM to server to browser, all streaming — is the architecture under every modern AI chat UI.

scenes.title: JWT auth in five lines. **Docs you never wrote.**

actors.t: docs are a side effect of the API

steps.at: Your API documentation is a side effect

scenes.narration: Auth: OAuth2PasswordBearer is FastAPI's built-in JWT pattern — declare it as a dependency, read the bearer token from the Authorization header, verify its signature and expiry, inject the user. RS256 versus HS256 matters at deployment: HS256 is a shared secret — one key signs and verifies, fine for a single service; RS256 is a key pair — the identity provider signs with a private key, your service verifies with the public one — so services can verify without holding signing power. Now the docs: every type hint and Pydantic model you've written has been feeding OpenAPI; FastAPI generates a full OpenAPI spec and a live Swagger UI at slash docs — interactive, try-it-now, always in sync with code. Your API documentation is a side effect of writing the API.

The docs point deserves emphasis because it changes behavior: when calling your API is a click away, frontend devs stop asking you questions and start building — the spec becomes a contract both sides trust. Generate typed clients from the OpenAPI spec and your Python backend types flow into a TypeScript frontend automatically. And the auth summary: for service-to-internal, HS256 with an env secret is fine; anything multi-service or user-facing should accept RS256 tokens from a proper identity provider — verify-only services never hold the private key. FastAPI gives you both: the bearer dependency for extraction, and your own verify function for the cryptography. Stage 5's backend pillar is complete — next, quality.

recap: Type-hinted function signatures ARE the contract: Pydantic validates requests/responses, bad input dies as 422 before your code
Depends() gives .NET-style DI with per-request caching, teardown via yield, and test overrides — inject db/vector store/LLM clients
SSE via EventSourceResponse streams LLM tokens to browsers; middleware + BackgroundTasks + /docs OpenAPI complete the production picture

quiz.q: Where does FastAPI request validation come from?
opts: Decorators you write on every route
Type hints + Pydantic models in the signature — constraints declared once validate automatically
quiz.why: The signature is the schema: Field(min_length=…), ge/le ranges etc. produce 422s with detailed errors — zero validation code.

quiz.q: What does dependency_overrides let you do in tests?
opts: Swap a dependency provider (e.g. get_current_user → fake user) without touching route code
quiz.why: Tests replace providers at the DI seam — the same seam production code uses, so the test exercises the real wiring.

quiz.q: Why use RS256 rather than HS256 when multiple services verify tokens?
opts: RS256 verifies with a public key — services can verify without holding the signing key; HS256's shared secret must live in every verifier
quiz.why: A shared signing secret in N services is N leak points; public-key verification means only the identity provider can sign.

code.title: A minimal production-shaped FastAPI skeleton
code.body:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sse_starlette.sse import EventSourceResponse

app = FastAPI(title="RAG Service")

class Ask(BaseModel):
    question: str = Field(min_length=3)
    stream: bool = True

async def get_store():
    async with VectorStore.connect() as vs:   # per-request, auto-close
        yield vs

@app.post("/ask")
async def ask(
    req: Ask,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    store: VectorStore = Depends(get_store),
):
    async def gen():
        async for token in rag.stream(req.question, store):
            yield {"data": token}
    return EventSourceResponse(gen())

# Run:  uvicorn app:app --reload
# Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs  ← Swagger UI, already complete
annot: get_store yields per request: connection lifetime matches request lifetime, exceptions included
user + store both injected: the route body is pure orchestration — dependencies carry the wiring
uvicorn is the ASGI server that runs the event loop; --reload for dev only

notes:
# FastAPI

## Routes & models
- Decorated functions = controllers; path/query params typed in the signature.
- Pydantic BaseModel: request validation + response shaping; 422s free.
- async def routes run on the event loop — await LLM/vector calls directly.

## Dependency injection
- `Depends(provider)`: per-request caching, chains compose, teardown via `yield`.
- `app.dependency_overrides[...]` in tests — swap at the seam.
- Inject db sessions, vector store, LLM clients uniformly.

## Middleware / background / streaming
- Middleware: request-wide concerns (request-id, timing). CORS: explicit origins.
- BackgroundTasks: fire-and-forget AFTER response — never for needed results.
- `EventSourceResponse` (SSE): re-emit httpx LLM streams to browsers.

## Auth & docs
- OAuth2PasswordBearer + JWT verify (RS256 for multi-service: public key verifies).
- OpenAPI + Swagger UI at `/docs`, generated from type hints.
- Run with uvicorn (ASGI). --reload = dev only.
